title: The Colonel's untouchables, the medics, and his brother's warning from Patton's army
summary: The Colonel kept him as an untouchable and transferred him to the Medical Corps, which he loved; his brother in Patton's army wrote telling him to avoid going overseas at any cost.

blocks.x: But as it turned out I went back to my regiment and the Colonel -- the Colonel had what everyone called untouchables. I was one of the Colonel's untouchables. When you came to get soldiers, he had a file on this side that was the untouchables, and there was a file on that side which was the touchables. I was one of the untouchables. So the Colonel transferred me to the medics. I became a member of the Medical Corps, which I loved. It was beautiful. I loved that sort of thing, you know. I found I loved it, you know. You've got to administer to the -- you know, like -- and I took first aid training. You know, you had classes every morning. You learned to draw a skeleton and point out the parts. You know, a real medical setup. And we had doctors. Doctors were Captains and Majors and Colonels. To teach the classes every morning. It was beautiful, that phase of it. Then we went on bivouac up in the mountains. We slept in tents. It was wintertime. I backed out of the tent one morning into 10 feet of snow. But at that stage it was fine. I loved it.
In the meantime I got a letter from my brother who was overseas, in General Patton's Army, and he said to me, "Whatever you can do to keep from coming overseas, you do it."

"Even if it means going to jail." He said, "You go to jail. Don't come over here." Because my brother went all the way across the channel, clean on to Berlin with General Patton, and he saw the worst of it. He came back from the war with six battle stars. Yes, sir.
